items.text: Better Dairy, a UK startup, is developing animal-free cheese and yogurt alternatives that aim to be healthier for consumers and better for the environment compared to traditional dairy products. Their goal is to create products that taste, melt, and stretch like regular cheese without involving cows. The company focuses on using precision fermentation to produce milk proteins, such as casein, that are essential for the texture and flavor of cheese. This process avoids the need for cows, reducing the environmental impact of dairy production. Traditional dairy farming produces methane, a harmful greenhouse gas, and uses large amounts of resources like land and water. Better Dairy is producing casein and another protein, osteopontin, at a small scale. However, they plan to increase production and are working on gaining regulatory approval in key markets, including the US. They hope to receive approval for casein by 2028 and osteopontin by 2027, which would mark a significant step in sustainable dairy alternatives. Difficult words: precision (exact or accurate), fermentation (the process of changing food using microorganisms), regulatory (relating to the control of an activity by a set of rules or laws). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Better Dairy is a UK startup which is working to create cheese and yogurt without cows. They make products in a way that is healthier for people and better for the planet. The company wants its cheese to taste, melt , and stretch like regular cheese without using cows. They use fermentation to create milk proteins like casein, which makes cheese taste and feel like the real thing. By doing this, they avoid the environmental problems of traditional dairy farming, such as methane emissions and using large amounts of resources, especially water and land. Better Dairy is making casein and another protein, osteopontin, in a small lab. They plan to increase production and hope to get approval to sell casein by 2028 and osteopontin by 2027. Difficult words: melt (to become soft or liquid by heat), fermentation (making food using microorganisms), avoid (to keep away from something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Better Dairy is a company from the UK. They are making cheese and yogurt without using cows. The cheese tastes and feels like real cheese, but it is better for the natural world. They use a special method called fermentation to make proteins like casein. Casein makes the cheese taste like real cheese. This method is good for the planet. It does not need cows. It does not need so much land and water. Right now, Better Dairy is making casein and another protein, osteopontin, in a small lab . They want to make more. They hope to get permission to sell casein by 2028 and osteopontin by 2027. Difficult words: fermentation (making food using microorganisms), lab (a room or building where experts do tests and experiments), permission (when you can do something because someone says yes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Consumer Electronics Show (CES) in Las Vegas showcased the latest health technology, focusing on prevention and data integration. Many devices, such as Withings’ health tracking system, collect personal health information and use artificial intelligence to analyze it. This data can help users understand their health better and even share insights with doctors. A hormone-measuring device allows users to track cortisol and progesterone levels through saliva testing. Over time, users will recognize patterns in their hormone levels, helping them make informed lifestyle decisions. Other innovations included non-invasive glucose monitors, smart rings, and advanced blood pressure cuffs predicting heart disease risks. There were also menopause-tracking devices using biological data rather than self-reported symptoms. A smart bed with built-in sensors monitors sleep, heart rate, and movement. It can also adjust positions for comfort, offer aromatherapy, and even contact emergency services if necessary. CES emphasized the importance of digital health tools in improving well-being. Difficult words: prevention (stopping something from happening), insight (deep understanding of something), cortisol (the body’s main stress hormone), progesterone (a female hormone that causes the womb to prepare for pregnancy), saliva (the liquid produced in your mouth to keep it wet and to help to prepare for food to be digested). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A show in Las Vegas presented new health technology which helps people prevent illnesses. One device collects health data and explains it using artificial intelligence. This information can help people understand their health and talk to doctors if they need it. Another company introduced a small tool to measure hormones in saliva . It helps users track their stress and hormone levels to improve their health. Other inventions included a smart ring, a blood pressure monitor to check heart disease risk, and a device to track menopause symptoms. A smart bed monitors sleep, heart rate, and movement. It can adjust for comfort and even call emergency services. The show focused on using technology to help people care for their health. Difficult words: prevent (to stop something from happening), saliva (the liquid in your mouth), invention (a new device, tool, or machine). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A show in Las Vegas shows new health technology. Some devices help people understand their health and talk to doctors. One machine collects health information and explains it. AI helps with it. People can understand their health better. Another small tool measures hormones in the mouth. It helps people see changes in their body and stress. Other new ideas include a smart ring, a blood pressure monitor, and a device for women’s health. There is also a special bed. It checks your sleep, heart rate, and movement. It can change position, make nice smells, and call for help. These things show that new technology can help people stay healthy. Difficult words: device (a thing made or adapted for a particular purpose), measure (to find out how big, or how much of something there is), blood pressure (how forcefully your blood goes through your body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Boom Supersonic’s XB-1 made history by becoming the first privately funded airplane to break the sound barrier during a test flight over the Mojave Desert. The flight reached Mach 1.1, 1,360 kph, faster than the speed of sound. Chief Test Pilot Tristan Brandenburg expressed his excitement, saying the plane had never flown better. This milestone is part of Boom Supersonic’s plan to create a commercial supersonic airliner called Overture. The Overture will carry 64-80 passengers and travel across the Atlantic in about 3.5 hours. The company already has 130 orders for the aircraft from major airlines, including American Airlines, United Airlines, and Japan Airlines. Boom Supersonic is constructing a new factory in Greensboro, North Carolina, where they plan to build 66 Overture planes per year. This successful test flight brings them one step closer to reviving supersonic air travel. Difficult words: milestone (important event or achievement), revive (to bring something back to life or use it again). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Boom Supersonic’s XB-1 broke the sound barrier during a test flight over the Mojave Desert. The plane reached Mach 1.1, 1,360 kph, faster than the speed of sound. The pilot, Tristan Brandenburg, said it was the best flight ever. This test is part of Boom Supersonic’s plan to make a commercial supersonic plane called Overture. The Overture will carry 64-80 passengers and travel across the Atlantic in about 3.5 hours. Boom already has 130 orders from American Airlines, United Airlines, and Japan Airlines. Boom Supersonic is also building a factory in Greensboro, North Carolina, where they will make 66 Overture planes every year. This test flight shows that they are getting closer to bringing supersonic air travel back. Difficult words: barrier (the limit), commercial (related to business), supersonic (faster than the speed of sound). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Boom Supersonic’s XB-1 breaks the sound barrier during a test flight over the Mojave Desert. The plane goes faster than 1,360 kph. The pilot, Tristan Brandenburg, says that it is the best flight ever. Boom Supersonic wants to make a supersonic plane called Overture. The Overture will carry 64-80 people. It will fly across the Atlantic in 3.5 hours. Big airlines like American Airlines and United Airlines want this plane. Boom Supersonic is also building a new factory in Greensboro, North Carolina. They want to make 66 Overture planes every year. This test flight brings back supersonic flying. Difficult words: barrier (the limit), flight (when something flies), supersonic (faster than sound). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Giant pandas are a favorite in zoos because of their playful and unique nature. They bring in large crowds and generate a lot of money for the zoos that host them. To have pandas, zoos must sign long-term contracts with China and pay over 1 million dollars annually per panda. Pandas only live naturally in China, so they hold both cultural and diplomatic value for the country. China uses ‘panda diplomacy’ as a tool to build relationships with other countries. However, this is not always positive. In 2023, when US-China relations became strained , China took back its pandas from two American zoos. Experts call this strategy ‘ punitive panda diplomacy.’ After negotiations, the pandas returned to Washington, DC, but analysts say this doesn’t guarantee stronger relations. China’s decisions about pandas depend on political circumstances, meaning they could withdraw them again. Difficult words: strained (difficult or tense), punitive (intended as punishment). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Giant pandas are very popular in zoos because they are fun to watch. People love to see them, and they help zoos make money. Zoos need to pay China over 1 million dollars a year for each panda. Because pandas only live naturally in China, they are very special to the country. China uses pandas for ‘panda diplomacy’ to make friends with other countries. Sometimes, China uses pandas to show its power. For example, in 2023, when China and the US had problems, China took its pandas back. Later, the pandas returned to Washington, DC, but experts say this doesn’t mean relations are better. China can decide to take them back if things change again. Difficult words: naturally (in nature, not because of people), diplomacy (managing relationships between countries), relation (a connection between countries or people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People love giant pandas. They are cute and fun to watch. So many zoos want them. Zoos pay China a lot of money every year to keep pandas. They pay 1 million dollars a year for each panda. China can do this because pandas live only in China. China uses pandas to be friends with other countries. But if China is not happy, it can take the pandas back. This happens in 2023 when China and the US have problems. China takes its pandas away. Now, pandas are back in Washington, D.C., but this does not mean China and the US are friends again. China may take the pandas back in the future . Difficult words: cute (nice to look at, sweet), future (the time to come). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Neura Robotics, a German company founded by David Reger, is at the forefront of robotics and AI technology. Their flagship product, the 4NE-1 humanoid robot, is designed for domestic and industrial tasks, and it is equipped with advanced AI, sensors, and the ability to mimic human touch. Reger, a former social worker with no formal engineering background, built the company with help from Swiss experts, Chinese funding, and later 100 million euros from Western investors. Neura relocated to Stuttgart, leveraging Germany’s strong mechanical engineering tradition. The company’s innovations include cost-effective welding robots and proprietary sensors that distinguish humans from machines. Neura employs 260 people from 35 nations and receives 2,500 job applications monthly. The company’s vision includes manufacturing 5 million robots by 2030, aiming to make robotics Germany’s leading industry, surpassing car manufacturing. Neura expects 50 million euros in sales this year, targeting India and other global markets. Difficult words: forefront (the leading or most important position or place), leverage (to use to maximum advantage), proprietary (unique and owned by the company). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Neura Robotics, led by David Reger, is a German company which creates cutting-edge robots. Their 4NE-1 humanoid robot can handle tasks at home and in factories. David, who started as a social worker, learned about robotics with expert help. He found support in China and later raised 100 million euros in Europe. Neura’s factory is in Stuttgart, where they focus on automation . The company makes cheap welding robots and develops sensors to identify humans. Neura employs 260 people from 35 countries and receives thousands of job applications each month. By 2030, they plan to make 5 million robots and expect 50 million euros in sales this year. Neura’s goal is to make robotics Germany’s top industry even bigger than cars. Difficult words: cutting-edge (very modern), automation (machines doing tasks without people), welding (joining metal parts together by heating). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Neura Robotics is a German company. They make robots for homes and factories. Their newest robot, 4NE-1, can do many tasks using smart AI. The company’s founder is David Reger. He starts as a social worker. He learns about robots with help from experts. He gets money from China first and later from Germany. Neura builds robots in Stuttgart, Germany, and makes things like welding robots. These robots save time and money. Neura also creates special sensors to tell people and machines apart. Neura has 260 workers from 35 countries and gets many job applications . By 2030, they plan to make 5 million robots. They expect €50 million in sales this year. They want robots to be Germany’s biggest industry. Difficult words: founder (a person who starts a company or business), sensor (a device which detects things like touch, heat, and so on), job application (a letter with details about your previous jobs and schools). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The world’s largest iceberg, A23A, is moving towards South Georgia, a remote British island known for its rich wildlife, including penguins and seals. This enormous iceberg broke away from Antarctica in December and is heading for ‘Iceberg Alley,’ where icebergs usually disintegrate . Scientists, sailors, and fishermen are monitoring its path through satellite images as they prepare for possible impacts. If A23A grounds itself near South Georgia, it could block the feeding grounds of many penguins and seals, endangering their survival. Similar events in the past have caused massive wildlife losses. However, the approaching iceberg represents both danger and a chance for valuable research. British researchers have studied the iceberg to learn about its effects on the ocean’s carbon cycle. Although A23A separated from Antarctica in 1986, it likely was not caused by climate change. However, scientists warn that climate change might increase the number of such giant icebergs in the future. Difficult words: disintegrate (to break into smaller pieces), ground (to come into contact with the ocean floor and stop moving), massive (exceptionally large). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The biggest iceberg in the world, A23A, is moving quickly toward South Georgia, a British island with many penguins and seals. This iceberg broke away from Antarctica in December and is now in ‘Iceberg Alley,’ a place where icebergs often break apart. Sailors, fishermen, and scientists are using satellites to follow it because it might block important feeding areas for animals. When such collisions happened before, they caused many birds and seals to die. Scientists are studying the iceberg to understand how it changes the ocean. This iceberg broke away a long time ago, so it may not be from climate change, but global warming could cause more icebergs like this in the future. It is dangerous for wildlife but also gives researchers an opportunity to learn. Difficult words: iceberg (a big piece of ice floating in the sea), feed (to give food to someone), opportunity (a chance of something happening). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big iceberg , A23A, is moving to South Georgia, an island with penguins and seals. A23A breaks away from Antarctica in December. People are watching it with satellites to see if it will hit the island. If the iceberg blocks the water, animals like penguins and seals cannot find food. This happens before, and many animals die. Scientists are studying the iceberg. They want to know how it changes the ocean. The iceberg starts breaking many years ago, so it is not because of climate change . But scientists think that more big icebergs may come in the future. A23A is dangerous for animals. At the same time, it helps scientists understand icebergs better. Difficult words: iceberg (a big piece of ice which floats in the sea), block (to make the movement or flow difficult or impossible), climate change (the world getting hotter). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Commission is testing social media platforms like Facebook, TikTok, and X to see if they are ready to handle disinformation before the upcoming German election. The test, scheduled for January 31, will assess whether these companies have the safeguards required by the Digital Services Act (DSA). Platforms including Microsoft, LinkedIn, Google, Snap, and Meta were invited, with TikTok confirming its attendance. This stress test involves evaluating how the companies would respond to possible scenarios where the DSA rules apply. Senior compliance officers and experts responsible for following the DSA will participate. The EU held a similar test last year for the European Parliament elections, which was considered successful. Now, they aim to work closely with German authorities to ensure platforms are prepared for risks during this national election. Difficult words: disinformation (false information spread to mislead people), safeguards (protections to keep something safe), stress test (a test designed to assess how well a system functions when subjected to greater than normal amounts of stress or pressure). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The European Commission wants social media companies, like Facebook and TikTok, to show they can stop disinformation before the German election. On January 31, there will be a test to check if these companies have the right protections , as the Digital Services Act (DSA) asks. TikTok said it would join, but other companies, like Google and Microsoft, didn’t say anything. The test will look at how companies handle different situations where the DSA rules are needed. Important officers and experts from the companies will take part. The EU already did a similar test last year before the European Parliament elections, and it worked well. This time, the test will also involve German officials. Difficult words: disinformation (false information shared to confuse people), protections (things which keep people or systems safe), involve (to include or contain as a necessary part). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Union is testing social media companies like Facebook and TikTok. The EU wants to check if they can stop fake news before the German election . The test will happen on January 31. TikTok said it will join. Other companies like Google and Microsoft do not say anything yet. The test will check how the companies follow the EU’s new rules , the Digital Services Act (DSA). Officers and experts will be part of the test. The EU does a similar test last year, and it goes well. This time, German officials will help with the test. Difficult words: fake (not real, not true), election (voting of a person for a job in politics), rule (what people or companies must do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Shares of European wind companies dropped after President Donald Trump suspended new federal offshore wind leasing. Trump claimed wind turbines are ugly, expensive, and harmful to wildlife. The global offshore wind sector has faced challenges, including rising costs and delays, and had hoped US policies under former President Joe Biden would support its recovery. Denmark’s Orsted, one of the largest wind power companies, suffered the most, with shares plunging 17%. The company announced a 1.69 billion dollar impairment charge on US projects, including the Sunrise Wind project, which had been set to become the largest US offshore wind farm. Analysts say Trump’s suspension made some Orsted assets in the US worthless. Other companies, like Portugal’s EDP Renovaveis, Germany’s RWE, and Norway’s Equinor, saw smaller declines in their stock prices. Difficult words: suspend (to stop something temporarily), plunge (to become lower in value or level very suddenly and quickly), impairment (a loss in value). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Shares of European wind companies fell after President Trump stopped new US offshore wind leasing. He said that wind turbines are ugly, costly, and harmful to animals. Wind power had problems with high costs and delays but got help from Biden’s green energy policies . Denmark’s Orsted got hit hardest, as its shares fell by 17%. The company took a 1.69 billion dollar loss on US projects, including Sunrise Wind, which was meant to be the largest US offshore wind farm. Experts said that Trump’s decision made some of Orsted’s US land useless. Other wind companies, such as Portugal’s EDP Renovaveis, Germany’s RWE, and Norway’s Equinor, also lost, but not so much. Difficult words: offshore (at sea), policy (ideas or an action plan), share (a part of a company which a person or another company can buy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

President Trump stops new US wind projects. He says that wind turbines look bad. They cost too much and are bad for animals. Denmark’s Orsted has the most problems. Its shares fall 17%. The company loses 1.69 billion dollars from US projects, including Sunrise Wind. Sunrise Wind should be the largest US wind farm. But now, some of Orsted’s US land is useless . Other wind companies, like Portugal’s EDP Renovaveis, Germany’s RWE, and Norway’s Equinor, also lose money, but not as much. Difficult words: wind turbine (a machine which makes energy from wind), share (a part of a company which a person or another company can buy), useless (something you cannot use or you cannot use it for what you want to). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Antibiotic resistance is a global health crisis, worsening due to misuse, with 30–50% of prescriptions being unnecessary. New tests involving a finger-prick test and throat swab offer hope. A finger-prick test identifies infection severity and likelihood of bacterial origin within 2–3 minutes, while a throat swab detects Group A Streptococcus with 100% accuracy. These might help doctors decide whether antibiotics are necessary and ensure precise treatment. Globally, such tests have reduced antibiotic use by up to 40–60%. A researcher from Deakin University in Melbourne is testing them locally to reduce misuse, guide doctors in prescribing antibiotics correctly, and assist governments in combating antibiotic resistance. If these tests prove cost-effective, they might be used widely and could help fight antibiotic resistance. Difficult words: resistance (the ability to resist treatment), swab (a small piece of soft material, often attached to a stick, used for collecting a sample from the body), precise (exact, accurate). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Antibiotic resistance is a big health problem worldwide because people use antibiotics too much or wrongly. Many prescriptions are incorrect because of the wrong type, amount, or time of use. To help, experts are trying new tests like a finger- prick test and throat swab . The finger-prick test shows how bad an infection is and if bacteria cause it. It gives results in 2–3 minutes, which means that doctors can decide quickly about what pills to use. The throat swab finds specific bacteria like Group A Streptococcus. Tests like these can lower the use of antibiotics by 40–60%. Although they are helpful, the finger-prick test needs more research to check its cost and use. If it is successful, these tools can reduce resistance and save lives. Difficult words: antibiotic re sistance (when antibiotics don’t work anymore), prescription (an instruction for a medicine), prick (to make a small hole in something with a sharp object), swab (a soft material on a stick which doctors use to get a sample from the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Antibiotics help people when they are sick. But using them too much is wrong. They stop working after some time, which is called resistance. New tests can help. A finger-prick test shows if an infection is bad and if bacteria cause it. It is fast. It gives answers in 2–3 minutes. A throat swab is a soft material on a stick. A doctor uses it to get a sample from the throat. It finds some bacteria, like Group A Streptococcus. It helps doctors choose the right pills. These tests may stop doctors from giving too many antibiotics. This can help people stay healthy. Scientists are studying these tests to see how they can work in different places. They can save many lives in the future. Difficult words: finger-prick (making a hole in your finger to get some blood), cause (to make something happen), sample (a small part which shows what something is like). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Elon Musk’s hand gesture during a speech at Donald Trump’s inauguration has caused widespread debate. At a rally in Washington, he slapped his chest and extended his arm outward, which some believe resembled a Nazi salute. The gesture quickly went viral, especially in Germany, where such actions are associated with Adolf Hitler and are illegal. Opinions on the gesture are divided. Historians argued it resembled the Nazi salute, while organizations like the Anti-Defamation League defended Musk, calling it an awkward gesture rather than a deliberate act. Musk dismissed the controversy on his X platform, stating critics needed ‘better dirty tricks.’ This controversy followed Musk’s recent support of Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. His endorsement shocked many, as AfD is labeled a suspected extremist party. Musk’s actions and comments, including mistakenly calling Hitler a communist, have raised concerns about his influence. Difficult words: deliberate (done intentionally), dismiss (to treat as unworthy of serious consideration), controversy (public disagreement or heated discussion), endorsement (the act of saying that you approve of or support something or someone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Elon Musk made a hand gesture during a speech at Trump’s inauguration, which caused debate . Musk touched his chest and extended his arm, which some say looked like a Nazi salute . In Germany, such gestures are illegal and connected to Adolf Hitler. People disagreed about the gesture. Some historians said it looked like a Nazi salute, but others, like the Anti-Defamation League, said it was not. Musk defended himself on X, saying critics were wrong. This happened after Musk supported Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. People see the party as extreme and anti-immigration. Musk also made a mistake when he called Hitler a communist, which made many people worry about his actions. Difficult words: gesture (when you move your hand to express something), debate (when people talk about something a lot), salute (a formal sign which soldiers usually do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Elon Musk makes a hand gesture during Trump’s speech . Many people are talking about it now. Musk touches his chest and moves his arm forward. Some people think that it looks like a Nazi salute . This gesture is illegal in Germany because Adolf Hitler makes it. Some people say that the gesture is bad. Others say that it is just a mistake. Musk says his critics are wrong. Before this, Musk likes a political party in Germany called Alternative for Germany (AfD). Many people think that this party is extreme. Musk also calls Hitler a communist, which is not correct. Many people are now worried about what Must will do next. Difficult words: gesture (when you move your hand to express something), speech (when someone talks in front of other people), salute (a greeting which soldiers usually use). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump issued 1,500 pardons, freeing hundreds of his supporters jailed for participating in the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot. Thousands had stormed the Capitol after Trump claimed the 2020 election was rigged . The violence resulted in five deaths, including a police officer, and left over 200 officers injured. The pardons included those convicted of violent crimes, leading to criticism from police, lawmakers, and some Republicans. This decision reversed the outcomes of the largest criminal investigation in US history. Fourteen individuals guilty of severe crimes had their sentences commuted , meaning they were released, but their convictions remained on record. Far-right leaders celebrated their release, labeling earlier sentences as politically motivated. The pardons also included those yet to be tried, ensuring they face no prosecution. This sweeping act sparked heated debate, with critics calling it unjust and supporters praising it. Difficult words: rigged (manipulated or controlled by dishonest means), commute (to change a punishment to a less severe one), sweeping (wide in range or effect). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Donald Trump pardoned 1,500 people connected to the attack on Capitol on January 6, 2021. Many people ended up in jail after storming the Capitol because Trump said the 2020 election was unfair. Five people died, including a police officer, and over 200 officers were hurt. Trump’s pardons even freed people convicted of serious crimes. Some Republicans and police criticized this decision, saying it was wrong. Fourteen people convicted of serious crimes had their sentences reduced, so they left prison, but their crimes stayed on record . Leaders of the riots celebrated. They believed that sending them to prison was unfair. Some people believe the pardons were unjust, but others think they were the right thing to do. Difficult words: pardon (to forgive a crime), storm (to get in a place with force), convicted (found guilty of a crime), on record (in a document which shows what happened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump forgives 1,500 people from jail after the Capitol attack. The attack happens on January 6, 2021. Many people take part in the attack because Trump says the 2020 election is not fair. Five people, including a police officer, died. Many people are hurt. The pardons free some people who do terrible things. This upsets police and some lawmakers. Fourteen people will stay in jail shorter than they should. Some leave jail, but their crimes stay in official documents. Leaders of the attack are happy. Some people believe the pardons are not fair, but others think they are the right thing to do. Difficult words: forgive (to say that someone’s mistake or crime is okay), pardon (to say that someone’s crime is okay), upset (to make someone angry or unhappy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Business owners in the leather industry in Indian-administered Kashmir are facing a crisis. A ban on cattle slaughter in 2014, coupled with the COVID-19 pandemic and reduced international demand, has left many tanneries struggling to survive. Prices for processed animal hides have dropped to less than a third of their former value, making it difficult for factories to cover basic expenses like wages and electricity. In 2014, the government banned cattle slaughter, leading to widespread losses when vigilantes targeted trucks carrying hides. Although the Supreme Court lifted the ban in 2017, the damage had already been done, and many tanneries had closed. Unemployment in the region remains three times higher than the national average. While the government promised support, people in the industry feel ignored. The importation of hides has worsened their situation by creating direct competition. Many leather workers hope for better policies, such as higher import duties, to support their trade. Difficult words: tannery (the place where leather is made), hide (animal skin used for leather), vigilant (a person taking law enforcement into their own hands). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The leather industry in Kashmir is in trouble. A ban on cattle slaughter in 2014, the COVID-19 pandemic, and low international demand caused big problems for tanneries . Prices for animal skins dropped a lot, and factory owners couldn’t pay for things like electricity and worker wages. The 2014 ban caused heavy losses. The top court lifted the ban in 2017, but many factories already closed. Now, unemployment in the region is three times higher than in the rest of India. The government promised to help the leather industry, but local business owners say things are still the same. They want higher taxes on imported animal skin to reduce competition . Many are waiting for change to save their business. Difficult words: slaughter (killing animals for food), demand (a need for products or services), tannery (the place where people make leather), competition (people or businesses trying to do better than others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The leather industry in Kashmir is having problems. In 2014, the government stops killing cows for food. COVID-19 and fewer international buyers make things even worse. Factory owners cannot pay for electricity or workers. The ban ends in 2017. Many factories must close before the ban ends. Now, many people in Kashmir do not have jobs. The government says that it will help. But business owners and workers say that nothing changes. They also have problems because imported animal skin makes it harder for them to sell their products. Workers hope that things will get better and they will not lose their jobs. Difficult words: leather (a material which comes from the skin of an animal), owner (a person who has something, and it belongs to him), imported (a thing which comes from another country and you can buy it in your own country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Greenland is closely following US developments after President Trump proposed buying the island. He claimed it would help American national security, especially against China and Russia. However, Greenland is self-governing and remains part of Denmark. Many Greenlanders oppose the idea, seeing it as offensive . They believe Greenland is not for sale. Trump is interested in Greenland’s vast resources, such as minerals and fishing opportunities. Greenland’s economy depends heavily on fishing, which makes up over 90% of its exports, and most people work in government jobs. Denmark supports Greenland with nearly 1 billion dollars annually, but some Greenlanders think they could survive independently by using their resources wisely. Debates about independence have increased in recent years, with many people wanting Greenland to manage its future. If independence happens, it might bring new challenges, like dealing with larger nations trying to exploit Greenland’s resources. However, Denmark has made it clear that selling Greenland is not an option. Difficult words: offensive (disrespectful), vast (of a very great extent or quantity), exploit (to make use of a situation in a way considered unfair). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

His films and TV shows, spanning nearly 50 years, entertained, thrilled, and mystified audiences with their imaginative worlds. Lynch’s artistic influence inspired generations, blending commercial filmmaking with true artistry. Fans and colleagues mourn the loss of a director who created magical, thought-provoking, and original cinematic experiences. Spain is leading efforts to make aviation more sustainable using biofuel derived from used cooking oil. This approach helps reduce environmental pollution and dependence on traditional fossil fuels. Customers at gas stations in Madrid can exchange leftover frying oil for fuel vouchers, and the collected oil is refined into kerosene at advanced facilities. These refineries turn the oil into a product chemically identical to petroleum-based fuel, making it fully compatible with airplane engines. Airlines such as Iberia aim to fuel 10% of their planes with biofuel by 2030, aligning with EU targets for increasing sustainable aviation fuel usage to 6% by 2030 and 70% by 2050. While biofuel costs about three times as much as traditional fuel, expanding production facilities, like a major refinery under construction in Andalusia, will help reduce costs. Tests by the German Aerospace Center reveal that planes running on biofuel emit fewer soot particles, resulting in fewer condensation trails which contribute to global warming. Spain’s efforts also include exploring other renewable raw materials to diversify sustainable fuel sources. These initiatives highlight the potential of waste, such as frying oil, to play a critical role in combating climate change. Difficult words: derive (obtain something from a specified source), leftover (something remaining after the rest has been used, especially food), kerosene (a fuel used for airplanes), soot (a black powder produced when coal, wood, or other material is burned). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol has been arrested after he attempted to impose martial law. This marks the first time a sitting South Korean president has faced arrest. Authorities had to force entry into Yoon’s residence using ladders and wire cutters. Yoon agreed to questioning at the Corruption Investigation Office to avoid violence, though he continues to call the investigation illegal. Yoon’s supporters protested strongly, even camping outside his residence in freezing weather, but they dispersed once news of the arrest spread. Yoon now faces charges of insurrection and will be held at Seoul’s Detention Center during the investigation. South Korea’s constitutional court must decide within 180 days whether to confirm his impeachment . If confirmed, a presidential election will follow within 60 days. Analysts view these events as a critical test of South Korea’s democracy. Difficult words: disperse (to separate), insurrection (a violent uprising against an authority or government), impeachment (a formal statement that a public official may be guilty of a serious offense). Tools like price alerts on apps like Skyscanner or Hopper can help you monitor flight costs. Even after booking, if ticket prices drop, you may be able to claim travel credits if you booked in certain ticket classes. Planning ahead and staying flexible can make your 2025 travel experience more affordable despite overall cost increases. Difficult words: lesser-known (not as well known as others of the same kind), off-peak (taking place at a time when demand is less), flexibility (the ability to change or adapt easily).
